findings.explanation: The grounding guide and Splunk_TA_nix use `sourcetype=linux_audit` for audit.log; this UC introduces `linux:audit` and the monitor stanza assigns it locally, so a host that already collects audit.log under the TA sourcetype would never match the IMA branch.
findings.quote: Optional near-real-time coverage uses `index=os sourcetype=linux:audit` records emitted by Linux IMA appraisal and written by auditd
findings.suggested_fix: Check which audit sourcetype Splunk_TA_nix assigns to /var/log/audit/audit.log and either use that sourcetype in the SPL and inputs.conf or state clearly that a second, differently named sourcetype is a deliberate local choice and how to alias it.

findings.explanation: The SPL calls `lookup linux_fim_authorized_changes host file_path detector ...` (a lookup definition name) while the text only describes creating `linux_fim_authorized_changes.csv`; no step creates the transforms.conf lookup definition or its permissions, so the lookup command will fail as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step to create the lookup table file and the matching lookup definition named `linux_fim_authorized_changes`, shared to the search app.

findings.explanation: The IMA branch depends on `type`, `op`, `cause`, `name` and `res` being extracted, but no add-on that supplies these extractions is named; the UC itself admits the parser may leave hex-encoded paths or numeric types, so the optional branch is less ready-to-run than the text suggests.
findings.quote: Optionally collect existing auditd IMA appraisal failures as `linux:audit`.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the audit parser/add-on expected to provide these fields, or mark the IMA branch as requiring local field normalisation before use.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Title 'Rootkit Detection via File Integrity' promises rootkit detection, while exclusions, description and implementation all state the UC cannot determine that a rootkit is present or absent and exclusions calls it a 'legacy title'. The title contradicts the body and overclaims.

Security UC with detectionType Baseline has no mitreAttack mapping at all (for example T1014 Rootkit or T1565.001 Stored Data Manipulation would fit the claimed intent); verify whether omission is intentional.

summary: Carefully hedged and technically detailed AIDE/IMA integrity-exception UC whose text repeatedly disclaims rootkit detection, but whose title still promises it. A few sourcetype and lookup naming details disagree with the grounding guide or leave the SPL non-runnable as written.
